solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Seek money from daughter to get possession of land

parts.note: to touch someone is slang for asking them for a loan or cash
to own something is to hold it as your property

explanation.surface: Someone cadges cash from their daughter in order to buy a plot of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' looks like a noun in the surface but is the verb, as an aircraft does.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft arriving on the ground is said to touch down, a phrasal synonym for landing.

clue.text: Subject of photo to stand at the front

indicators.note: tells us the word to is placed before the other piece rather than after it

parts.note: taken as written
pic is a casual short form of picture, i.e. a photo

explanation.surface: The person photographed is asked to stand at the front of the group.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject under discussion is a matter or theme, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Last religious leader accepted union's final terms

parts.note: ult., short for ultimo, means of last month in old business letters

indicators.note: the religious leader takes in, or accepts, the union, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an imam leads prayers in a mosque
TU stands for trade union; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A cleric at the end of negotiations agrees to the trade union's closing demands.
explanation.walkthrough: ULT is the commercial abbreviation of ultimo, meaning last month.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultimatum is a last demand whose rejection ends talks, so it is a set of final terms.

clue.text: In early October, Irish could be affected

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into another word, signalling a reshuffle

parts.note: Oct, the opening of the month's name, is its usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: Something Irish might be influenced by events at the start of October.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges IN + OCT + IRISH; 'affected' is the adjective meaning theatrical, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Histrionic behaviour is melodramatic and showy, so it is affected in the sense of put on.

clue.text: Sick woman ate last bits of sushi without thinking

indicators.note: the shuffled word eats, taking the other letters inside itself
sick here means unwell or disordered, so the letters of woman are jumbled

parts.note: the final two letters of sushi are H and I

explanation.surface: A woman felt ill after finishing off her sushi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick' reads as the woman's illness but signals the rearranged letters ONAWM; 'ate' makes them swallow the sushi's final pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on impulse, with no deliberation, is acting spontaneously, an idiomatic equivalent.

clue.text: Protesters' opposition to excavations is supported by European candidate

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece rests on, or is supported by, the next

parts.note: a protest placard against digging would read No Mine

explanation.surface: Demonstrators against mining are backed by a European candidate for office.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the upper piece is 'supported by' the lower, so E comes after NOMINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person put forward for election or an award is a candidate, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Left son to go round in a bad mood

indicators.note: turning round means the pair of pieces is read from right to left

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A son abandoned to go about in a sulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go round' turns PORT + S backwards. A strop is British slang for a sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a strop is British slang for sulking or being in a temper, i.e. a bad mood.

clue.text: Active agent closes in on Resistance

indicators.note: the spy closes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A secret agent tracks down members of the Resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry describes someone lively and nimble, especially an older person, so active in body.

clue.text: Implicated in obscure Belarussian revolt

indicators.note: the letters are caught up inside the following words, spanning them

explanation.surface: An unknown citizen of Belarus is involved in an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebel is to rise up against authority, a verb synonym for revolt.

clue.text: Priest subjected to abuse over article carried the day

indicators.note: the reviled word covers, or lies over, the article, enclosing it

parts.note: reviled means abused with insults
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A clergyman was insulted about a newspaper piece he had written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts A inside REVILED; 'article' is grammatical, not a newspaper story.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry the day is to win, and to prevail is likewise to triumph, an idiomatic equivalent.

clue.text: Beginning to protest at his heartless ways

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word is its first letter
with its heart, the middle letter, removed only the outer letters remain

explanation.surface: A protest begins against a man who is unfeeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Paths and ways are both routes or tracks for travel, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Wrongly blamed IRA for being worthy of respect

indicators.note: wrongly means in error, so the letters are set out incorrectly

explanation.surface: Someone unjustly blames the Irish Republican Army for an incident.
explanation.definitionFit: Admirable qualities deserve esteem, so the word means deserving respect.

clue.text: Appreciate non-selective school set back her goal

parts.note: a comp, short for comprehensive, is a British state school admitting pupils of all abilities

indicators.note: set backwards, so the little word is read in reverse

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A state school delays a girl's ambition, which she is meant to accept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' turns HER into REH. A comprehensive is a British state school taking all abilities.
explanation.definitionFit: To appreciate something can mean to grasp or understand it fully, the sense used here.

clue.text: Plenary starts with a petition

indicators.note: only the opening stretch of the word is kept, the rest dropped

explanation.surface: A full session of an assembly opens with a formal request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' keeps PLE, the start of Plenary, dropping NARY.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an earnest request or appeal, as is a petition.

clue.text: Means of getting information from a digital company

parts.note: thumbs are digits, read here as belonging to the digit family
a crew is a company of workers, as on a ship

explanation.surface: A tech firm offers a way to obtain data.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital' suggests computing, but it is about the digits of the hand; the 'information' is extracted by torture.
explanation.definitionFit: This torture device squeezed the thumbs to extract confessions, so it was a grim tool for getting information.

clue.text: You and I finally get space in the shower area

parts.note: together you and I are we

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of the next word

parts.note: room means available space

explanation.surface: Two people at last have room in the bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet room is a fully waterproofed bathroom with an open shower, so it is a shower area.

clue.text: Trying habit is nothing to me

parts.note: a habit is a garment, something to wear, as a monk's habit
O resembles zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone declares that a certain custom means nothing to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' is a monk's or nun's dress, i.e. clothing or wear, not a routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trying taxes your patience, and wearisome means tiresome in just that way.

clue.text: Just one found in the confused state

indicators.note: the single letter is found inside the other pieces
confused means muddled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for the US state of California
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: One fair-minded person is discovered amid a muddled nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' scrambles the little word into ETH; 'found in' places the numeral one after it. 'Just' is the adjective meaning fair, not 'only'.
explanation.definitionFit: Just as an adjective means morally right and fair, matching ethical.

clue.text: Workmate has depression over extremely loathsome fever

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece written above the next

parts.note: a col is a dip between two mountain peaks

indicators.note: the extremes of the word are its first and last letters

parts.note: ague is an old name for a malarial fever

explanation.surface: A fellow worker is depressed after a nasty bout of fever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' is a geographic dip, not low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A colleague is a person you work alongside, so a fellow worker.

clue.text: Tramp is ill-treated in undesirable locations

indicators.note: ill-treated means abused or knocked about, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A homeless man is mistreated in rough parts of town.
explanation.definitionFit: An armpit is slang for an unpleasant, squalid place, as in the armpit of the world.

clue.text: Sneer regularly at immorality that may occur in church

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, picking every other letter

parts.note: vice is wicked or immoral conduct

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at wickedness that might happen even in a place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A church service is a gathering for worship, an event which takes place in a church.

clue.text: Quietly spoken man fell apart after losing credit

parts.note: M is a standard abbreviation for man or male

indicators.note: losing means the named letters are taken away

parts.note: something crumbled when it fell to pieces
CR is the accountancy abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A man broke down after his credit ran out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops CR from CRUMBLED to leave UMBLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumbled words are uttered indistinctly and low, so they are spoken quietly.

clue.text: Height of folly to end up in a large crowd

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a mass is a large crowd of people

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written bottom to top

explanation.surface: It is the height of foolishness to finish inside a huge throng.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns END into DNE, which goes 'in' MASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Madness is utter foolishness, so it can be called the peak or height of folly.

clue.text: Unoccupied French island shelters half the party

indicators.note: the island shelters the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: ile is French for island

indicators.note: half of the word is kept, its second letter cut

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: An empty French island gives refuge to half of a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' trims DO to D, which the island 'shelters'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means not working or in use, so unoccupied.

clue.text: High Latin frequently found in poems at the end of the century

parts.note: oft is a poetic, archaic word for often

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Elevated Latin often turned up in verse written at the turn of the century.
explanation.definitionFit: Lofty means tall, towering or elevated, so it means high.

clue.text: Brightly coloured flower gets boy to return with money

indicators.note: the flower gets, or receives, the next piece inside it

parts.note: the iris is a garden flower

indicators.note: to return means to come back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Ed is a boy's name, short for Edward
a cent is a coin, a unit of money

explanation.surface: A flower sends a boy back with some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' gives DE from the boy's name; the flower 'gets' it inside. 'flower' is a bloom here, not a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Iridescent surfaces shimmer with rainbow colours, like oil on water, so they are vividly coloured.

clue.text: Mexican leaders pursue the idea

indicators.note: the leaders come after, or pursue, the other word, so they go second

parts.note: the leading two letters of Mexican are M and E

explanation.surface: Heads of Mexico chase after a concept.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the central subject or idea of a work, a near synonym.

clue.text: Rate of progress by sea bird

definitions.meaning: a nautical mile per hour, the unit of speed at sea
a small wading sandpiper of shores

explanation.surface: How fast a seabird travels.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the unit of ship's speed and the name of a sandpiper.

clue.text: Push off before I have followed directions

indicators.note: this word sits ahead of the rest of the pieces

parts.note: E, N and S are compass directions: east, north, south
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone tells a person to go away, having been given instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Push off' looks like one phrase; 'Push' alone is the definition, a military offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A military offensive is an attack or big advance, also called a push.

clue.text: Non-standard parachute has no opening

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a drogue is a small parachute used to slow or stabilise

explanation.surface: A faulty parachute fails to open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no opening' drops the first letter, D, from DROGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue example deviates from the norm, as a rogue wave or rogue value, so it is non-standard.

clue.text: Say why announced exercise is in North Africa

parts.note: eg, for example, means say

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word's sound gives a letter

parts.note: the word why is said like the letter Y
PT is physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a workout is happening in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The country is located in the north-east of Africa, so it is a place in North Africa.

clue.text: Otherwise, we imprison that woman in a different location

parts.note: else means otherwise, as in or else

indicators.note: we lock the other piece inside, enclosing it

parts.note: her refers to a woman already mentioned

explanation.surface: Otherwise we lock her up somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means somewhere other than here, a phrasal equivalent.
